findings.condition: The no-plans state of AC-058 is scanned with axe only for Chile. AC-060's verification asks for the automated scan for Colombia and Chile in each listed state, the no-plans message included.
findings.description: Verification gap against the AC text, not a defect in the product. Recommendation: deactivate Colombia's plans in plan-changes.spec.ts as well and run expectNoAxeViolations, or have the owner accept the one-country mapping.
findings.impact: A WCAG violation that appears only in Colombia's no-plans state would go undetected. The risk is low because the code path is the same and both countries share the theme. The approved plan (plan.md AC-060 row, T013) mapped only the Chile scan.

findings.condition: The production initial bundle is 753.38 kB raw (162.49 kB transfer), against a warning budget of 500 kB and an error budget of 1 MB.
findings.description: Not a regression of this change. Recommendation: capture it as a FUT, for example lazy-loading Zod-heavy paths or raising the budget with a reason, so the warning does not become noise.
findings.impact: This warning predates the change: the CHG-001 runs already measured 747.63 kB, and this change adds about 5.75 kB. The build passes, and the size is well below the error budget.

findings.condition: The choice button's accessible name is a computed aria-label, '{chooseLabel|chosenLabel}: {plan name}'. The approved prototype instead appended a visually hidden ': {name}' span.
findings.description: Accepted as a reasonable deviation. Optional: use the prototype's sr-only suffix so translation tools handle it the same as visible text.
findings.impact: The resulting accessible name is the same as the prototype's. It starts with the visible text (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name), includes the plan name (AC-060) and keeps aria-pressed for the chosen state (AC-048). Plan D11 asks only for an accessible name that includes the plan name, so this is a choice of technique, not a change of behaviour. Minor caveats: some browser auto-translation tools skip aria-label, and the ': ' separator is fixed in code.

findings.condition: Before every axe scan, including the CHG-001 scans, the shared fixture now waits for all finite Web Animations (for example the transition-colors of a button that just changed state) and skips infinite ones such as the spinner.
findings.description: Accepted as a sound change to the test harness. No action needed.
findings.impact: Axe now measures contrast at rest instead of mid-transition, which removes false positives without hiding real steady-state violations. A finite but very long animation would hold the test until its timeout and fail it, so a problem would not pass silently.

findings.condition: The public find and findOne on plans return every published plan, inactive ones included, when called without the active filter (the e2e support reads them that way).
findings.description: Recommendation for the content guidance: plans that must stay confidential should be kept as drafts, not just inactive. An alternative is a later decision to force active=true on the public plan controller, which needs an architecture update.
findings.impact: A plan the business team publishes but marks inactive, for example an upcoming plan with its price, is publicly readable through the API although the wizard never shows it. This matches AC-066 and the architecture reference (find and findOne on read types), so it is not a defect.

findings.condition: priceQuoteRequestSchema accepts any whole number for the ages, negative or very large values included, and plan identifiers of any length up to Strapi's JSON body limit.
findings.description: Recorded as reviewed attack surface. Optional hardening: bound the ages (for example -1 to 150) and the plan id length in the shared schema.
findings.impact: Nothing leaks: the endpoint is stateless, stores and logs nothing, answers only a bracket-based simulated price for a public plan, and returns fixed error texts. Out-of-range ages only fall into the extreme brackets.
